highlights.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?
highlights.summary: As uncertainty swirls over the boss of the AI chip giant, some names have emerged as potential successors.
body: Nvidia is facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang.

The chief executive and co-founder of the AI chip-making giant is at the centre of a major scandal over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
But finding the right person to lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into the world's second most valuable company - after Apple - is a challenge.
We take a look at which candidates have emerged as potential successors.

highlights.title: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex
highlights.summary: With Codex, Holiday Extras is turning customer expertise into better apps, higher booking conversion and new possibilities for growth.
body: Holiday Extras ⁠ (opens in a new window) helps customers search, book and manage trips. For CEO Matthew Pack, becoming an AI-based travel technology business means changing how the whole organisation works: giving the people who understand customers and operations the ability to improve them directly.

Company-wide ChatGPT Enterprise access established the foundation. Codex extended it into building software, from customer-facing apps to internal systems. Pack builds with Codex himself, using that experience to understand what colleagues need and raise his expectations of what the business can achieve.

Holiday Extras had spent years developing its mobile apps ⁠ (opens in a new window). Major changes to its main app centred on an annual release. With Codex, it challenged itself to rethink the experience and how it was built.

body: Michael Carrick has been dismissed by Manchester United. He departs after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford last Sunday that left the team in the Premier League’s bottom three. United twice fought back from two goals down for a late point against Villa, after a dramatic recovery to defeat Roma in the Champions League five days earlier, but that wasn’t enough.

United are third-bottom in the Premier League, a point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and 17th in the Champions League league phase table. His departure follows a review led by the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy.
“ Are we a bit late to the party with Pochettino?” wonders Paul Scholes on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.
“I actually think he’s a brilliant appointment... he could be perfect... but I’ve got that slight concern we are not getting his best years.”

highlights.title: CD Projekt Red Will Use AI to Bring Back Geralt’s Original Voice
highlights.summary: In 2019, Jacek Rozenek, the Polish voice actor for Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher games, suffered a stroke that greatly affected his speech. He underwent extensive training to recuperate and regain his ability to act. However, the changes in his voice were still noticeable.
body: If you played the English version of The Witcher 3, Doug Cockle will immediately spring to mind when you think of Geralt of Rivia. However, in the game's original version, Geralt is played by Jacek Rozenek, a renowned voice actor with 30 years of experience. CD Projekt has hired Rozenek to play Geralt of Rivia since the original The Witcher game in 2007, and the Polish studio wants him to continue in the role for Songs of the Past. Unfortunately, the actor suffered a stroke in 2019, that, according to Game File, left him unable to speak for months.

After extensive rehabilitation, Rozenek was able to speak again, but his voice was not the same. Stephen Totilo wrote, "it was lower, gruffer," after an interview with the actor. CDPR concluded that while this voice change might work well for an older Geralt in The Witcher 4, it wouldn't blend well with the voice you hear in The Witcher 3. Coming out next year, the Songs of the Past DLC is set in the same era as the main game, and the two are closely connected. This means that fans will hear newly recorded lines and older lines in close succession. To solve this problem, CDPR is working with AI voice cloning company Respeecher.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

body: The government is prepared to force the entertainment industry to improve safeguarding practices unless rapid change is introduced, BBC Newsnight has learned.
Participation in the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA) is currently voluntary.
It comes after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News alleged that entertainer David Walliams had been accused by several women of sexual misconduct and abusing his position, which he denies.
Nandy said earlier this week that she was summoning leaders from the broadcasting, publishing, film and entertainment industries to "draw a line" in the sand.

highlights.title: I’ve had a stinking cold this week – and I’m longing for good advice | Adrian Chiles
highlights.summary: Heavy and light colds tend to pass more quickly than middle-of-the-road ones. But should I stay in bed or continue mixing with others? How to define the cold that’s ruining your day? There’s a hierarchy. We start with the sniffle, the mere runny nose, scratchy throat or just feeling a little off.
body: The only good thing about the stinking cold is that you have the green light to do sod all and repair to bed. This was me for three days this week, and it has firmed up a theory I have long held that you’re better off getting a stinker because it tends to come and go and be done with more quickly than the other varieties. This theory, I should point out, is based on my lived experience rather than any clinical expertise or any kind of research. Sorry – I felt too ill to bother with anything of the kind.

The kind of cold I really can’t bear is the middle-of-the-road, magnolia, vanilla, neither-here-nor-there type. When you don’t feel up to doing much, but neither, if you’re honest, are you feeling ropey enough to justify doing nothing. And these kinds of colds, for me anyway, seem to drag on for ever.

But seriously, what do you do? What’s the right call for your own health and for others in your workplace or friendship group? Do you stay at home for the greater good, or do you soldier on bravely and be quietly commended for toughing it out, while running the risk of infecting friends, enemies and workmates with a dose of whatever you’ve got?

highlights.title: Ring confirms its camera drone won’t have manual controls after crashing on CBS News
highlights.summary: When (or if) Ring's security camera drone flies into our homes in January, you won't get the option to pilot it yourself. The Ring Drone Cam relies entirely on an "AI Pilot" system to follow pre-programmed routes and navigate autonomously around obstacles, with no manual control option available …
body: The Ring Drone Cam will entirely rely on AI autopilot to fly around your home.

The video, broadcast on CBS Mornings and published on Threads, shows Ring founder Jamie Siminoff allowing technology reporter Jo Ling Kent to manually fly an early version of the drone via a mobile app with integrated controls.

The demo then shows the drone crashing twice while being manually piloted. In the first instance, Ring reportedly told CBS News that the drone’s collision avoidance technology malfunctioned, and declined to share the video recorded by the drone prior to crashing. CBS News caught the second crash on camera, with the footage showing the drone colliding with a wall after failing to respond to manual controls. According to Siminoff, this occurred because the drone lost internet connectivity — which it also relies on to fly autonomously.
“If it loses connectivity, it’s supposed to stop and land,” Siminoff said in the video. “It did not there.”

highlights.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
highlights.summary: MIT scientists developed a training method to generate models that simulate the effects of human activities on climate much more quickly than other approaches.
body: Accurate, up-to-date climate projections are essential for planning decisions that enhance the resilience of power grids, protect public health, maximize agricultural yields, and more.
Now, MIT researchers have developed a technique that streamlines the production of fast, trustworthy, and adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction.
These specialized AI models, known as climate emulators, can rapidly simulate the effects of human activities onto a future climate, predicting impacts on temperatures or sea level, for example.

Because emulators run in a matter of seconds, scientists use them to efficiently test thousands of varied climate scenarios. This provides more reliable estimates and can identify unexpected outcomes of regional interventions.

highlights.summary: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente denies claims Lamine Yamal received "special privileges" after being allowed to join the national team later than the rest of the squad.
body: The 19-year-old did not travel with Spain for Thursday's Nations League match against the Czech Republic because of discomfort and inflammation in his right knee following Barcelona's La Liga victory over Atletico Madrid, remaining in Barcelona to work with the club's medical staff.
"I decided that, to avoid the trip, it would be better for him to stay at home and continue treatment with his club," De la Fuente said on Wednesday.
"Lamine [Yamal] doesn't have any special privileges. We would have done this for any other player.
"What hurts me most is the lying, the lack of rigour, the absence of truthfulness and the fabrication. I can't stand people who try to deceive you and lie."

highlights.title: Nvidia board considering ousting CEO Jensen Huang, report claims, as news of a second affair comes to light
highlights.summary: Nvidia's board of directors has reportedly met to decide whether to remove the company's embattled CEO Jensen Huang, as news of a second extramarital affair has come to light.
body: Per the Wall Street Journal, the board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang following reports he allegedly participated in another affair with an executive who worked for him. This followed the revelation of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which prompted a company-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation into whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

The board's decision has yet to be made, but there are three expected outcomes. Either Huang stays with the company and continues as Nvidia leader, despite the controversy or he is replaced as CEO, or he quits. Nvidia's share price dropped following reports of this meeting taking place.

If Huang is fired - and perhaps even if he isn't - it's likely to severely disrupt Nvidia's operations. Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it to become one of the world's most valuable companies - it interchangeably wears that crown, alternating with Apple. Replacing Huang might change the company's focus.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Tom Holland Says Starring in ‘The Odyssey’ Has Given Him an ‘Ambition to See What Else is Out There For Me’
highlights.summary: Tom Holland has starred in two of this year’s biggest-grossing films – “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” – but he says it’s the latter that will impact the next stage of his career.
body: “I’ve been an admirer of Chris since I can remember, and to have the opportunity to work with him and to have his approval, and to sit in his house and watch his movie and to get a pat on the back, for me, just was like the perfect way for me to start whatever it is that I’m doing next,” Holland explained. “He’s given me a level of confidence as an actor that I don’t know if I had before and I’m very grateful that that is something that I can take away from this.”

Holland said that while he has also learned a lot from his fellow actors (which included his wife Zendaya) and crew members, he would be going into his next project “with this sense of achievement and this newfound confidence in what I think I can do” thanks to Nolan’s film. “That is what Chris and Emma do so well, is they really champion their actors,” he said.

The actor, who has played Spider-Man for over a decade, is understood to be in pre-production for a Fred Astaire biopic which will see him return to his dancing roots, given that Holland’s entry into showbiz was via the West End stage production of “Billy Elliot.”

highlights.title: NHS England deletes ‘misleading’ claim 137 trusts benefiting from Palantir AI tools
highlights.summary: Exclusive: The Guardian revealed 29 hospital trusts were not or hardly using the controversial patient data tech. NHS England has deleted a claim from its website stating 137 hospital trusts are benefiting from Palantir’s AI health data system after the Guardian revealed 29 of them were not using…
body: Health bosses had published a list of all the NHS bodies “live” with and “realising benefits” from the AI-powered federated data platform (FDP), a system set up to improve patient outcomes, boost operating theatre efficiency and speed up bed discharges. But after 29 trusts said it was either not live or they were not using any of its applications, the original list of hospitals appears to have been taken down.

The move comes as ministers weigh up whether to extend Palantir’s £330m contract to 2029 and after the Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR) said it was examining the NHS claims about the extent of the system’s use, which critics say make it appear more embedded in the health service than it actually is.

A less detailed page now says early users were “already seeing real results – reduced admin, faster patient pathways, and more time for care”. A senior Labour MP, calling for the contract to be scrapped, warned the move threatened public trust.

highlights.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
highlights.summary: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children’s safety. The work supports shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.
body: OpenAI pledges $2 million as part of a global effort to better understand AI’s impact on children and support their safety and wellbeing.

Earlier this week at the Paris Peace Forum, OpenAI signed the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI for Children ⁠ (opens in a new window) and committed $2 million to support the scientific research network under the Coalition for Children’s Rights and Protection in the Age of AI.

This builds on our call for global standards on youth AI safety, and sustained collaboration among governments, researchers, civil society and industry to translate shared evidence into practical safeguards.

Our contribution supports shared measurement work: developing tools researchers can use to better understand and measure AI’s risks and opportunities for children, helping inform safer products and better policy.

highlights.title: Amy Hennig's Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra hasn't been cancelled, Skydance reportedly says, as rumours swirl to the contrary
highlights.summary: You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.
body: Reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku says, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly," Gigliotti reportedly told staff. "There is no truth to these claims."

This follows a recent rumour that the action adventure title was potentially going to get the axe in the near future. The rumour originated from a Marvel 1943 fan account, and while the original X post has since been deleted, it didn't stop it from spreading online, including amongst the game's own development staff.
According to Kotaku's report, Rise of Hydra is close to its alpha state, despite seemingly five years of development. The game is said to have had multiple issues through its long development.

highlights.summary: "We're not making mobile games this time," says former Hutch boss Shaun Rutland.
body: The founding team behind Top Drives and F1 Clash developer Hutch has raised $5m to build a new company focused on interactive generative video.
Anorak’s pre-seed round was co-led by Play Ventures and Backed VC, with Supercell and MTG also taking part. Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron is among the angel investors.

The startup is led by CEO Shaun Rutland, who co-founded Hutch before MTG acquired it for $375m in 2020, and chief creative officer Jonathan Alpine, who held the same role at Hutch. David Amor is COO, and cofounder Tak Fung runs the company’s AI lab in Chengdu, China. Anorak now has a team of 20 across London and Chengdu.
As we reported last week, Rutland has been teasing Anorak through his blog, describing it as a studio focused on “interactive generative video”.

Directed by William Eubank (“Underwater”), “Ghost Soldier” stacks up one-man-army cliches as early as the opening credits and continues as if…
body: William Eubank's patriotic exercise casts the 'Sound of Freedom' star as a former Special Forces man defending his small Wyoming town from foreign corporate overlords.

Jim Caviezel, who’s increasingly made himself a Hollywood representative for politically conservative ideologies with projects like “Infidel” and “Sound of Freedom” (not to mention a series of faith-based projects that began with “The Passion of the Christ”), does little to dispel that association as this film’s tireless, technologically advanced and morally upright title character. But Eubank’s glossy direction, paired with a merciless urgency (and complete lack of originality) in Chris Papsadero’s script, renders the story’s ripped-from-the-headlines details with too little dimensionality even for it to deliver the satisfaction of a good, bloody B-movie.

highlights.title: ‘A web of canals and cobbled streets’: a city break in Haarlem in the Netherlands
highlights.summary: A short ride from Amsterdam, this laid-back city has great museums, cosy bars and a new exhibition featuring the works of Rembrandt and local artist Frans Hals this winter.
body: I t’s only 15 minutes away from the Dutch capital by train, but Haarlem feels a million miles from Amsterdam, and perhaps provides a more typical glimpse of the Netherlands than trailing around the well-worn tourist trail of Van Gogh, coffee shops and red lights. An attractive city of cobbled streets, gabled houses and canals, Haarlem is, as the Dutch would say, a gezellig sort of place – cosy, convivial, and full of intriguing nooks and corners. I’ve been coming here for years, and it seems odd that Haarlem is not better known, at least to UK visitors.

This winter there’s the added draw of an exhibition devoted to the works of a local boy, the 17th-century painter Frans Hals, and his better-known contemporary Rembrandt in the city’s Frans Hals Museum (until 28 February 2027). No one really knows whether these two titans of the Dutch Golden Age of the 16th and 17th centuries ever met, but seeing their work hung together like this is powerful and compelling. The museum used to be the Oudemannenhuis (Old Men’s House), a retirement and care home where Hals lived out his final penniless years.

body: When Palantir chief executive Alex Karp sat down with Politico this week, he reportedly used the word “progressive” eight times to describe both his political philosophy and his company.

“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life,” Karp told Politico, which noted that he called the Democratic Party “ totally irresponsible ” in the distant time of October 2025. “I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir—all of our products are essentially progressive.”

This isn’t the first time Karp has called himself a progressive. In 2018, The New York Times reported that Karp described himself as such. In the same article, he claimed to have voted for Hillary Clinton.

Karp has also donated money to Democratic candidates. In 2023, for instance, he donated $360,000 to a joint fundraising committee for Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. The next year, he donated $1 million to MAGA, Inc.

highlights.summary: Midfielder’s old-school attributes came to the fore during Nottingham Forest’s win against Manchester City. Modern football is more systematised and data-driven than ever but some things never change.
body: Nottingham Forest’s 3-1 win against Manchester City last weekend featured a classic example. Forest led 2-1 inside the last 20 minutes but City, lifted by Rayan Cherki’s sweet half-volley, were pushing for an equaliser.
Another City attack comes down their right: after Jair Cunha’s clearing header from a deep Matheus Nunes cross, the ball loops up in the air before descending inside the home penalty area.

Ryan Yates, Forest’s old-fashioned midfield general, is being pressed from behind by the Argentina international Enzo Fernández as the ball drops. Yates stands his ground, using his strength to hold off his opponent’s muscular challenge. Fernández tries to impose himself, too, but ends up on the turf.

Not only does Yates win that crucial one-on-one, by cleverly improvising an overhead kick to shift the ball away from danger he inadvertently begins a counterattack that arguably changes the course of Forest’s season.

highlights.title: 7 Greatest Live-Service Games Killed Before Their Time, Ranked
highlights.summary: At one point or another, most of us have enjoyed a live-service game. Likewise, many of us have been burned when a game publisher decided the revenue no longer justified the ongoing expenses of maintaining an always-on experience. Suddenly, we had nothing to show for our time except memories.
body: Plenty of games reach that point after giving off warning signs. Maybe they never got big enough to last. Maybe they became huge, but then they faded away rapidly as audiences lost interest. Some live-service games were killed before their time, however. They deserved better, and we’re here to remember them.

The extended Final Fantasy franchise has included a number of live-service games. Despite the brand recognition, those efforts haven’t always fared well, even when they should have. For me, Mobius Final Fantasy is the best example of unmet potential.

First launched in Japan on June 4, 2015, the game lasted just shy of five years in that region and less than four in North America. It was originally a mobile-only title, noteworthy in part because of the involvement of producer Yoshinori Kitase and scenario supervisor Kazushige Nojima. The two Final Fantasy veterans helped assemble a compelling new take on the classic original Final Fantasy, featuring Garland and blank-slate Warrior of Light characters, among others.

The name, however, more or less translates as “little tender one”, although that “little” refers more to the fact that it is a bit tender, rather than being on the small side. Especially because tenerina recipes from Ferrara call for tins ranging from 24-26cm in size, which produce slender cakes that are gently cracked on top and tacolenta (sticky) within; in fact, another name for the cake is torta tacolenta.

A timer is to forgetful cooks what a microwave is to melting chocolate: that is, invaluable. Otherwise, use a bain-marie or bowl balanced over (but not touching) simmering water in a pan. It is an important step to separate the eggs, so they can be added in two stages. First the yolks beaten with the sugar; then the whites beaten to stiff peaks and folded in gently to protect the air that’s been so carefully incorporated. Regarding the flour, it can be substituted for ground almonds, hazelnuts or pine nuts, all of which produce an almost identical texture, alongside lovely flavour; they also turn the cake into what could be called a torta caprese.

highlights.title: Google Wanted Spirit Airlines Data. Flight Attendants Found a Way to Opt Out
highlights.summary: The union representing flight attendants for the defunct airline struck a deal with Google to scrub sensitive employee records from a $10 million data sale.
body: If you care about privacy, don’t feed your own personal information into a chatbot, which—among other concerns—could use it to train AI tools. Employees, though, mostly don’t have a choice.

A new, multibillion-dollar industry is dedicated to selling and buying work files and emails to companies seeking fresh sources of data to improve their AI models, and it’s only getting bigger. Data privacy laws tend to focus on consumer protections and rarely consider the rights of workers who create that information. What happens when your doctor’s notes, employee contracts, and Slack gossip are fed into the machine?

An agreement reached this week between Google and a union representing an unlikely workforce—flight attendants—could reveal a more permanent answer by creating a process that might reliably separate the data that workers produce from their own personal information. A judge still needs to approve the agreement next week.

body: Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI.

I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck— please hurry up and ship it, guys —but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing. I plan to have the robot automatically dispense a treat for my pet bengal, Leona, perhaps by bowing its head to release one from a 3D-printed, head-mounted storage chamber.

I was able to code and train the virtual robot in just a few hours, which is, quite frankly, incredible. Previously, this kind of thing might have taken me weeks to figure out. It was possible because OpenAI’s latest models are remarkably good at understanding and manipulating 3D representations of the physical world and then translating that into useful code, agentic actions, and robot training.

The delicate, spaghetti-strapped design featured a pale silver-gray windowpane check, a fitted bodice scattered with tiny beaded flowers, and a voluminous floor-skimming skirt. She accessorized with Swarovski Matrix hoop earrings—a recent favorite—and traded the flipped bob she’s been sporting of late for a sleek micro ponytail, tied with a little ivory ribbon. highlights.title: Andy Baraghani's Ditto Cafe Is His Most Personal Project Yet
highlights.summary: The former BA editor spent years tailoring his cooking for everyone else. A Ditto, his NYC counter-service café, he’s finally serving food entirely on his own terms.
body: Andy Baraghani is more afraid of becoming stagnant than he is of dying. Stagnancy, he’s quick to clarify, is different from stillness. Stagnancy is like a fetid pond; stillness is meditative. Baraghani seems to be at risk of neither.

It is late morning on the first actually chilly day of autumn and we are staring one another down across a stainless-steel prep table, which has been dragooned into use as an island in his outrageously good-looking kitchen. He is about to make me scones—salty-sweet ones with dates and lemon zest, an offering under development for his forthcoming café Ditto. But first, we’ll need to pop out for cream.
Quite literally in motion since I arrived, Baraghani finishes his point on stagnancy: He fears a life in which he is not learning, moving, or evolving “as a writer, a cook, and a good gay,” he says.

points: The Rockets defeated the Warriors, 115-105 tonight in Houston.
Kevin Durant finished with a team-high 20 points along with 5 assists and 4 rebounds for the Rockets, while Alperen Sengun tallied 19 points, 13 rebounds and 9 assists in the game.

The Rockets improve their record to 9-3 with the win, while the Warriors fall to 8-4 for the season.

points: The Trail Blazers defeated the Thunder, 118-108 tonight in Portland.
Deni Avdija contributed a team-high 28 points to go with 6 assists 4 steals and 4 three pointers, with Jrue Holiday of the Trail Blazers adding an additional 19 points (5-12 FG, 5-8 3P) in the game.
